Danish Energy Agency and Energinet (2026). Technology Data - Generation of Electricity and District Heating, version 0019 (latest amendment August 2026; first published August 2016). ISBN 978-87-94447-55-3. Danish Energy Agency, Copenhagen. www.ens.dk/technologydata. Data sheets: technology_data_for_el_and_dh (alldata long workbook, version 0019).

Guideline (p.25): financial data in real 2020 EUR excl. VAT and taxes. Workbook Intro: cost data in 2020 EUR except datasheets 22x, 40x, 41x, 45x and 47x in 2025 EUR; the 40/41/45/47 sheet headers say 'Cost data in 2025 EURO'. The 22 PV sheets carry no header; recorded as 2025_EUR per the Intro, although their note N lists an inflation index relative to 2020 ('Prices (EUR-2020)') - REVIEW. alldata_long 'priceyear' column says 2020 for every sheet, which contradicts the Intro for 22/40/41/45/47.

Produced by _high/_work/scratch-dea_2026_technology-data-electricity-district-heat/extract.py from the individual datasheets of the workbook (not alldata_long: its 40 Comp. hp, airsource 10 MW COP and nameplate rows (2.7/2.5) differ from the datasheet (2.8/2.6); all other 17,000 values agree). Scope: industry-relevant heat and CHP technologies only - 59 datasheets: 01 coal extraction CHP, 04/05 gas turbines (simple cycle with heat recovery, combined cycle), 06 gas engines, 08 waste-to-energy CHP and HOP, 09 biomass CHP (back-pressure and extraction) and HOP, 10 Stirling gasified biomass, 11 SOFC and 12 PEM fuel-cell CHP, 20 onshore wind (utility; for the wind-turbine gap), 22 commercial/industrial rooftop PV+BESS (for the photovoltaic-array_battery-storage gap), 40 compression heat pumps, 41 electric boilers, 44 gas and 47 oil DH boilers, 45 geothermal DH with heat pump, 46 solar DH, 50-52 peak plants. Skipped: 02 life-time extension and 03 coal-to-biomass conversions (power-plant retrofits), 21 offshore wind, other 22 PV sheets, 20 domestic turbines, 23 wave. Base year: 2025 where the sheet prints a 2025 central value (20, 22, 40, 41, 45, 47), else 2020 (all other sheets; no 2025 column). Lower/upper loaded as value-min/max only when printed for the same year: 2020 sheets have 2020 ranges; the 2025 sheets 40/41/45/47 print ranges only for 2030 and 2050, so they have no range; 20 onshore prints ranges for 2020 only. Ranges equal to the central value are dropped. All other years go to _projections.csv (the DEA convention in this folder). Loaded: capacity (MW_e electric-output for CHP and power; MW_h thermal-output for heat-only), net annual-average electrical and heat efficiency (target electricity/heat for CHP; blank target for heat-only, = COP for heat pumps), name-plate efficiency only where no annual average is printed (01 coal, 10 Stirling), lifetime, construction time, minimum load, availability/capacity factor/degradation where printed, CH4 and N2O per GJ fuel input (CO2 is not printed), capex = Nominal investment (*total) per MW (M EUR/MW x1000 to EUR/kW), fixed O&M (EUR/MW/y /1000 to EUR/kW-yr), variable O&M per MWh output (for heat-only sheets with a split, the 'other O&M' row, i.e. excluding the auxiliary electricity cost). Derived: heat-to-power-ratio = 1/Cb (Cb printed; back-pressure mode); efficiency-chp = electrical + heat annual average for back-pressure CHP (report note H: total efficiency is their sum); PV capacity factor = AC full-load hours/8760; temperature-output from the DH forward temperature in the sheet title (40, 45 and large 08/09 sheets). Flows: auxiliary electricity per GJ heat for heat-only boilers and solar DH (not included in their efficiency, guideline p.23); for heat pumps and geothermal it is inside the COP (notes D/M) and goes to _other-values. _other-values: name-plate efficiencies, equipment/installation splits, per-MW-input and per-tonne-input costs of biomass/WtE CHP (note J: not additive to the per-MW_e cost), outages, Cb/Cv, condensate, fuel-storage cost, start-up costs, geothermal well and heat-pump split, PV/battery details. Not extracted: SO2/NOx/particles (non-GHG), regulation and start-up times, space requirement, binary design flags, per-DC PV rows. Locators: 'report p.N' is the PDF page, which equals the table-of-contents page numbers (pages carry no printed number); the 11 SOFC and 12 PEMFC chapters are not in the v0019 report (datasheets only). All efficiencies of thermal plants are on LHV (guideline p.22); emissions per GJ fuel at LHV (p.25). COST BASIS overnight = EPC/overnight price incl. on-site infrastructure, excluding owners' costs and interest during construction (guideline p.25-26); onshore wind is total-plant (includes land, neighbour settlements, decommissioning of old turbines and construction loan interest, note H).
